items.title: ChatGPT for Teens Is Not Safe for Kids, Common Sense Media Report Says
items.author: Rachel Metz
items.content: <article>OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens — which the company rolled out in August as the default way for kids ages 13 to 17 use its popular chatbot — is too risky for children, according to a new report from Common Sense Media.</article>

items.title: SpaceX Eyes $40 Billion Deal to Buy Nvidia Chips
items.content: <article>Elon Musk’s SpaceX is in talks with banks and investors to raise $40 billion to buy chips from Nvidia, people familiar with the matter said. Pimco is one of the investment managers looking at the deal, according to the people. Bloomberg's Anthony Stephens reports. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Elon Musk Rules Out Potential TSMC Role in Terafab Operations
items.author: Debby Wu
items.content: <article>Elon Musk said his business empire will build and operate Terafab independently, quashing speculation about industry leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. swooping in to run his ambitious chipmaking venture.</article>

items.title: South Korea’s Nuri Rocket Lifts Off With Hanwha Aerospace Help
items.author: Soobin Kim
items.content: <article>South Korea launched its homegrown Nuri rocket for a fifth time, with the expanded involvement of defense contractor Hanwha Aerospace underscoring the increasing reliance on the private sector to boost the country’s space ambitions.</article>

items.title: JPMorgan's Guven Toktamis on Private Equity DPI & Outlook
items.content: <article>Pressure to show strong distributed paid-in capital (DPI) is top of mind in the private equity space, says Isik Guven Toktamis, JPMorgan EMEA Head of Private Equity Investment Banking. "2026 has been actually been a good year for sponsored M&A. Overall, M&A volume is up by 40%, and we continue to have a very strong pipeline, of exits," she added. Guven Toktamis spoke with Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie at the JPMorgan Tech Stars Conference in London on Oct. 6. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ServiceNow President and COO Amit Zavery on AI Demand
items.content: <article>ServiceNow's Amit Zavery remains bullish on the broader AI sector, citing strong enterprise demand for AI-powered software. The President and COO says ServiceNow continues to outperform its financial targets, thanks to a favorable outlook. He speaks with Haslinda Amin on the sidelines of Token2049 in Singapore. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Coinbase's Martin Sees Rising Demand for Crypto
items.content: <article>Liz Martin, Coinbase Institutional's co-CEO, says demand for crypto assets and tokenization continues to grow, driven by greater regulatory clarity and increased transparency. She speaks on the sidelines of Token2049 in Singapore.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Viture CEO Sees Smart Glasses Moving Beyond Smartphones
items.content: <article>David Jiang, CEO of Viture, says smart glasses still have low market penetration, and their future growth depends on reshaping the way people interact with computers. He speaks on the sidelines of the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Dragonfly’s Qureshi: Easy Money in Crypto is Over
items.content: <article>Haseeb Qureshi, Managing Partner at Dragonfly, says the crypto market is in a period of consolidation, with retail investors beginning to pay attention again. He speaks on the sidelines of Token2049 in Singapore. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Former Canadian Intl Trade Minister on Global Trade, AI
items.content:
<article>Mary Ng, Former Canadian Minister of International Trade and Milken Institute Senior Fellow, discusses her outlook AI's role in trade and investments in the region, and how Canada can work more with partners in Asia to foster opportunities for growth.
She speaks with Avril Hong on the sidelines of the Asia Milken Summit in Singapore on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)</article>
